stimuli.text: The temperature of a liquid, in degrees Celsius, is modeled by a differentiable function $$H$$ of time $$t$$, in minutes. Selected values are shown.
Water flows into a tank at a rate of $$R(t)$$ gallons per minute, where $$R$$ is a continuous function of time $$t$$ in minutes. Selected values are shown.
The function $$g$$ is differentiable. Selected values of $$g$$ are shown.
Let $$R$$ be the region enclosed by the graphs of $$f(x) = 3\cos\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)$$ and $$g(x) = x^2 - 2$$.

A particle moves in the xy-plane so that for $$0 \leq t \leq 3$$, $$\frac{dx}{dt} = 2\sin\left(\frac{t^2}{4}\right) + 1.5$$ and $$\frac{dy}{dt} = \cos(t)\,e^{t/4}$$. At $$t = 0$$ the particle is at $$(3, 3)$$.
The continuous function $$f$$ is defined on $$0 \leq x \leq 6$$. Its graph consists of line segments, as shown. Let $$g(x) = \int_{2}^{x} f(t)\,dt$$.
A particle moves along the x-axis with velocity $$v(t) = 3t^{2} - 18t + 15$$ for $$t \geq 0$$. At time $$t = 0$$ the particle is at $$x = -5$$.
People enter an amusement park at a rate modeled by a differentiable function $$P$$, where $$P(t)$$ is measured in people per minute and $$t$$ is measured in minutes. Selected values are shown.
A function $$f$$ has derivatives of all orders. Selected values are $$f(2) = 1$$, $$f'(2) = -5$$, $$f''(2) = -5$$ and $$f'''(2) = 5$$. For all $$x$$, $$|f^{(4)}(x)| \leq 30$$.

questions.stem: Let $$f(x) = \begin{cases} kx - 6 & x < 3 \\ x^{2} - 3 & x \geq 3 \end{cases}$$ where $$k$$ is a constant. For what value of $$k$$ is $$f$$ continuous at $$x = 3$$?

questions.stem: What is the radius of convergence of $$\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{n\,(x - 2)^n}{4^n}$$?

rubric.criterion: Uses $$g'' = f'$$, the slope of the segment.

parts.prompt: On the open interval $$0 < x < 6$$, find all values of $$x$$ at which $$g$$ has a relative maximum. Justify your answer.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the correct values (or that there are none).
Justifies using a sign change of $$g' = f$$ from positive to negative.
rubric.example: $$g' = f$$ changes from positive to negative there.

parts.prompt: Find the absolute maximum value of $$g$$ on $$0 \leq x \leq 6$$. Justify your answer.

rubric.criterion: Considers the endpoints and every critical point (Candidates Test).

parts.prompt: At what times does the particle change direction? Justify your answer.

rubric.criterion: Gives both times with a sign-change justification.

parts.prompt: Is the speed of the particle increasing or decreasing at time $$t = 7$$? Give a reason.

rubric.criterion: Finds the velocity and acceleration at the time.

rubric.example: Same signs, so the speed is increasing.

parts.prompt: Find the position of the particle at time $$t = 7$$.

rubric.criterion: Uses the initial position and an antiderivative of $$v$$.

parts.prompt: Find the total distance traveled by the particle from $$t = 0$$ to $$t = 7$$.

rubric.criterion: Splits the motion at the turning points.

questions.title: Rate of people entering a park

parts.prompt: Use the data to estimate $$P'(7)$$. Show the computations and indicate units.

rubric.criterion: Uses a difference quotient on the interval containing the time.

parts.prompt: Use a trapezoidal sum with the four subintervals shown in the table to approximate $$\int_0^{12} P(t)\,dt$$. Explain the meaning of this integral in the context of the problem.

rubric.criterion: Sets up the trapezoidal sum with unequal widths.

rubric.example: The total number of people who enter the park during the first 12 minutes.

parts.prompt: Must there be a time $$c$$, for $$3 < c < 9$$, such that $$P'(c) = 0$$? Justify your answer.

rubric.criterion: Answers yes, citing the Mean Value Theorem (or Rolle's Theorem) with its conditions.
rubric.example: Yes. $$P$$ is differentiable (so continuous), and $$P(3) = P(9) = 44$$. By the Mean Value Theorem there is a $$c$$ with $$P'(c) = \frac{44 - 44}{6} = 0$$.

parts.prompt: Must there be a time $$t$$, for $$0 < t < 3$$, at which $$P(t) = 35$$? Justify your answer.

rubric.criterion: Answers yes, citing the Intermediate Value Theorem and continuity.
rubric.example: Yes. $$P$$ is continuous, and $$35$$ is between $$P(0) = 27$$ and $$P(3) = 44$$, so the IVT guarantees such a $$t$$.

parts.prompt: Write the third-degree Taylor polynomial for $$f$$ about $$x = 2$$.

rubric.criterion: Uses the correct coefficients, including factorials.

parts.prompt: Use $$P_3$$ to approximate $$f(2.5)$$.
Use the Lagrange error bound to show that the approximation in part (b) differs from $$f(2.5)$$ by at most $$\frac{5}{64}$$.

rubric.criterion: Writes the Lagrange bound with the given M.

parts.prompt: Write the second-degree Taylor polynomial for $$f'$$ about $$x = 2$$.

rubric.criterion: Differentiates $$P_3$$ (or uses the derivative values directly).
